lessons.name: CIA Triad & Security Principles
lessons.desc: Confidentiality, integrity, availability — the three pillars every security control maps back to. Includes defense in depth, least privilege, and fail secure.
lessons.q: Explain the CIA triad. How does each principle apply to a real-world system you have designed?
lessons.qsub: How do defense in depth and least privilege complement the CIA triad? When would you choose fail secure over fail open?
terms: Sirf authorized log data dekh sakein (encryption, access control).
Data unauthorized change na ho (hash, signature, checksums).
Service jab chahiye tab chale (redundancy, DDoS protection).
lessons.what: Definition: CIA triad security ke teen stambh hain. Har control inme se kisi ek ko protect karta hai. Saath mein: defense in depth (kai layers), least privilege (minimum access), fail secure (fail ho to deny).
lessons.why: Design review mein poochho: kaun sa C/I/A risk hai? Isse controls ka priority tay hota hai.
lessons.code:
# Example mapping
Confidentiality -> TLS, AES-GCM, RBAC
Integrity       -> HMAC, digital signatures, DB constraints
Availability    -> multi-AZ, rate limiting, backups

# fail secure
if (!authz.check(user, action)) return 403   // error par bhi deny
where: SOC2/ISO controls CIA se map hote hain.
cons: Trade-offs: zyada confidentiality kabhi availability ghatati hai
gotchas: Fail open sirf safety-critical cases (fire door) mein
Ek control se saare teen cover nahi hote

lessons.name: Authentication vs Authorization
lessons.desc: Authentication verifies identity ("who you are"). Authorization determines access ("what you can do"). Factors: something you know, have, are. Common failure: checking AuthN but forgetting AuthZ.
lessons.q: What is the difference between authentication and authorization? Why do engineers confuse them?
lessons.qsub: Compare RBAC, ABAC, and ReBAC. When would you choose each model for a system you are designing?
terms: Tum kya kar sakte ho — permissions.
401 = identity nahi pata; 403 = pata hai par allowed nahi.
lessons.what: Definition: AuthN pehle (password, MFA, token), AuthZ uske baad har request par (RBAC, ABAC, ownership check). Dono alag layers par implement hote hain.
lessons.why: Zyada tar breaches authN bypass se nahi, authZ missing hone se hote hain (IDOR/BOLA).
cons: AuthZ logic scatter ho jaata hai
gotchas: Authorization har request par, sirf login par nahi

lessons.name: Cryptography Basics
lessons.desc: Symmetric (AES-256-GCM), asymmetric (ECDSA, Ed25519), hashing (SHA-256, bcrypt), and digital signatures. AEAD encrypts and verifies integrity together.
lessons.q: Compare symmetric and asymmetric cryptography. When would you use AES-256-GCM vs RSA?
lessons.qsub: Why is bcrypt preferred over SHA-256 for password hashing? What is authenticated encryption and why does it matter?
terms: Ek hi key: AES-256-GCM (fast, bulk data).
lessons.what: Definition: Symmetric data encrypt karta hai; asymmetric key exchange aur signatures ke liye; hash integrity ke liye. Passwords ke liye slow hash (bcrypt/argon2) aur salt, SHA-256 nahi.
lessons.why: Apna crypto kabhi mat likho — vetted libraries aur safe defaults use karo.
gotchas: IV/nonce kabhi reuse mat karo (GCM mein catastrophic)

lessons.name: PKI & Certificate Management
lessons.desc: Hierarchy of Certificate Authorities (CAs) that trust each other up to a root CA. TLS certificate chain validation, CRL, OCSP, Let's Encrypt, and Certificate Transparency.
lessons.q: Explain how the TLS certificate chain works. What happens when a certificate is revoked?
lessons.qsub: Compare CRL and OCSP. What is OCSP stapling and why does it improve performance and privacy?
terms: Trusted authority jo certificate sign karti hai.
lessons.what: Definition: PKI mein browser root CAs par trust karta hai; server leaf cert + intermediates bhejta hai. Cert mein domain, public key, expiry aur CA ka signature hota hai.
lessons.why: Expired/misconfigured certs outages ka bada kaaran hain; automation (ACME/Let's Encrypt) zaroori.
lessons.code:
$ openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -issuer
$ certbot renew --dry-run          # auto-renew test
cons: CA compromise ka risk, renewals ka bojh
gotchas: Intermediate chain missing ho to kuch clients fail
Private key kabhi repo/logs mein nahi

lessons.name: Threat Modeling
lessons.desc: STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation of privilege) maps threats to components. Attack trees model multi-step paths. Risk = likelihood × impact.
lessons.q: How do you perform threat modeling on a new system? Walk through the STRIDE framework.
lessons.qsub: How does PASTA differ from STRIDE? What tools (OWASP Threat Dragon, Microsoft TMT) help automate threat modeling?
terms: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation.
Jahan data ek trust level se dusre mein jaata hai.
Data flow diagram — threat model ka base.
lessons.what: Definition: Threat modeling design stage par poochta hai: Hum kya bana rahe hain? Kya galat ho sakta hai? Kya karenge? Kya hum ne sahi kiya? DFD banao, trust boundaries mark karo, har element par STRIDE lagao.
lessons.why: Design mein fix karna code mein fix karne se bahut sasta hai.
lessons.code:
Element: Login API (crosses internet → app boundary)
S: credential stuffing -> rate limit + MFA
T: token tamper -> signed tokens
R: no audit -> log auth events
I: verbose errors -> generic errors
D: brute force -> throttling
E: role claim edit -> server-side role lookup
gotchas: Ek baar ka document nahi — design badle to update
Sirf attackers nahi, insider threats bhi
Mitigation ko owner aur ticket do

lessons.name: OWASP Top 10
lessons.desc: The most critical web application security risks: Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Security Misconfiguration, and more.
lessons.q: Name the current OWASP Top 10. Which three are most common in modern web applications?
lessons.qsub: How do Broken Access Control and Security Misconfiguration differ? What automated tools detect these issues?
lessons.what: Definition: OWASP Top 10 web apps ke sabse common risks ki list hai (Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Misconfiguration, Vulnerable Components, Auth Failures, Integrity Failures, Logging Failures, SSRF).
lessons.why: Interview aur audits ka common vocabulary; checklist ki tarah code review mein kaam aata hai.
lessons.code:
// Review checklist (snippets)
- Har route par authZ?
- Parameterized queries?
- Secrets env/vault mein?
- Dependencies updated (npm audit)?
- Security headers (CSP, HSTS)?
- Auth events logged?
gotchas: Order har edition mein badalta hai
API ke liye alag OWASP API Top 10
Sirf list yaad karna kaafi nahi — fix patterns jaano

lessons.name: XSS Deep Dive
lessons.desc: Stored XSS (saved on server), Reflected (in URL), DOM-based (client-side). CSP (Content Security Policy) prevents all three. Output encoding must be context-aware.
lessons.q: Explain the three types of XSS. How does Content Security Policy prevent each?
lessons.qsub: Why is innerHTML dangerous? How do you implement context-aware output encoding in HTML, JavaScript, and URL contexts?
terms: Payload DB mein save, sabko trigger.
Browser ko batata hai kaun si scripts allowed.
lessons.what: Definition: XSS mein attacker ki JS victim ke browser mein tumhari site ke origin par chalti hai — cookies/tokens chura sakti hai. Fix: output encoding, framework auto-escape, CSP, HttpOnly cookies.
lessons.why: XSS = full account takeover; origin ka trust attacker ke haath mein.
gotchas: HttpOnly se cookie chori rukti hai, XSS nahi
Blacklist filter kaam nahi karta — encode karo

lessons.name: CSRF & SameSite Cookies
lessons.desc: CSRF tricks a victim into performing actions on another site. Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookie attribute (Lax, Strict, None) provide browser-level protection.
lessons.q: How does a CSRF attack work? What defenses would you implement in a modern web app?
lessons.qsub: Compare SameSite=Lax, SameSite=Strict, and SameSite=None. When would you use each?
terms: Victim ke browser se authenticated request attacker trigger kare.
Cookie cross-site requests mein nahi jaati (Lax/Strict).
lessons.what: Definition: Browser cookies automatically bhejta hai, isliye evil.com se bank.com par POST ho sakta hai. Defense: SameSite=Lax/Strict, anti-CSRF tokens, Origin/Referer check, custom header for APIs.
lessons.why: State-changing endpoints (transfer, password change) ke liye critical.
lessons.code:
Set-Cookie: sid=abc; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

<form method="post">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="{{token}}">
</form>
// server: token session se match karo
pros: SameSite se bahut hadd tak automatic
gotchas: GET se state change mat karo
Bearer token header wale APIs par CSRF nahi hota
XSS ho to CSRF token bhi chura sakte hain

lessons.name: SQL Injection & NoSQL Injection
lessons.desc: SQLi injects malicious SQL through input fields — UNION-based, error-based, blind. NoSQLi targets MongoDB/Couchbase with $where and $regex. Parameterized queries are the fix.
lessons.q: Explain blind SQL injection. How do you detect and prevent it?
lessons.qsub: How do ORM frameworks protect against SQLi? What happens when you use raw queries in an ORM?
terms: Input se query ka structure badal jaye.
lessons.what: Definition: String concat se query banane par attacker ' OR 1=1 -- daal ke logic badal sakta hai. Fix: prepared statements/ORM parameters, least-privilege DB user, input validation.
lessons.why: Data breach ka classic aur ab bhi common raasta.
cons: Dynamic identifiers par parameters kaam nahi karte
gotchas: ORM raw queries mein bhi risk

lessons.name: SSRF & IDOR
lessons.desc: SSRF makes the server fetch internal resources (cloud metadata endpoints). IDOR lets attackers access resources by changing IDs. Both require server-side validation and authorization checks.
lessons.q: How would you exploit SSRF to steal AWS IAM credentials? How do you defend against it?
lessons.qsub: Why are UUIDs not a security control? How do you properly implement authorization checks to prevent IDOR?
terms: Server ko attacker ke diye URL par request karwana.
ID badal ke dusre ka data.
lessons.what: Definition: SSRF mein server internal services/metadata (AWS IMDS) tak request bhej deta hai. Fix: URL allowlist, private IP block, IMDSv2, egress filtering. IDOR: ownership check missing.
lessons.why: Capital One breach SSRF se hua — cloud credentials leak.
gotchas: Redirects follow karne se allowlist bypass
Predictable ids ko UUID karna fix nahi — ownership check chahiye

lessons.name: XXE — XML External Entity injection, XXE mitigation
lessons.desc: XXE attacks exploit XML parsers that process external entities. Attacker injects XML entities to read local files, SSRF, or cause DoS. Mitigation: disable DTD processing, disable external entities. JSON APIs are not vulnerable. Only affects XML-based systems (SOAP, SAML, SVG, DOCX).
lessons.q: What is XXE and which systems are vulnerable? How do you prevent it?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between XML external entity and XML internal entity? How do you disable XXE in Java and Python?
terms: Document Type Definition jisme entities define hoti hain.
lessons.what: Definition: XXE tab hota hai jab XML parser external entities resolve karta hai. Attacker local files padh sakta hai, SSRF kar sakta hai ya DoS (billion laughs).
lessons.why: XML/SOAP/SAML/SVG/docx uploads sab XML parse karte hain — chhupa hua attack surface.
lessons.code:
<!-- payload -->
<!DOCTYPE r [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>
<r>&x;</r>

// Java fix
factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true);
// Python: defusedxml.ElementTree.parse(f)
cons: Parser defaults purane libraries mein unsafe
gotchas: JSON API ho to bhi Content-Type switch se XML parse ho sakta
Sirf external entities nahi, DTD hi band karo

lessons.name: SSTI — Server-Side Template Injection, auto-escaping, sandboxing
lessons.desc: SSTI occurs when user input is embedded in a template without escaping. Attacker injects template syntax to execute code server-side. Jinja2, Twig, Handlebars, FreeMarker all vulnerable. Mitigation: auto-escaping, sandbox mode, never render user input directly.
lessons.q: What is SSTI and how do you detect it? What is the impact of SSTI in Jinja2?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between SSTI and XSS? How do you sandbox a template engine?
terms: User input template code ban jaye.
lessons.what: Definition: Agar user input ko template string mein concatenate karke render karo (render_template_string("Hello " + name)), attacker {{7*7}} bhej ke code execution tak ja sakta hai.
lessons.why: SSTI aksar seedha RCE hota hai — server poora compromise.
lessons.code:
# Bad (Jinja2)
render_template_string("Hello " + request.args['name'])
# Good: data context mein pass karo
render_template_string("Hello {{ name }}", name=request.args['name'])
# Probe: {{7*7}} -> 49 ho jaye to vulnerable
pros: Fix: user input kabhi template nahi
gotchas: Auto-escape SSTI nahi rokta (XSS rokta hai)
User-editable templates ko logic-less engine (Mustache) mein rakho
Sandbox par poora bharosa mat karo

lessons.name: Directory Traversal — path traversal, null bytes, URL encoding
lessons.desc: Directory traversal uses ../ sequences to access files outside the web root. Bypasses: URL encoding (%2e%2e%2f), null bytes (%00), double encoding. Mitigation: validate paths against whitelist, use chroot/jail, never use user input in file paths directly.
lessons.q: What is directory traversal and what are common bypass techniques?
lessons.qsub: How do you prevent directory traversal in Node.js and Python? What is the null byte attack?
terms: Path resolve karke base ke andar check.
lessons.what: Definition: /download?file=../../etc/passwd se attacker web root ke bahar ki files padh leta hai. Fix: filename ko ID se map karo, ya resolve karke base directory prefix verify karo.
lessons.why: Config files, keys aur source code leak ho sakte hain.
gotchas: Check decode ke baad karo, pehle nahi
Zip-slip: archive entry names bhi validate

lessons.name: Open Redirect — parameter manipulation, SSO bypass, phishing
lessons.desc: Open redirect: application redirects user to attacker-controlled URL via manipulated parameter. Used in phishing (legitimate domain → malicious site), OAuth/SSO bypass, token theft. Mitigation: validate redirect URLs against whitelist, use callback URLs.
lessons.q: What is an open redirect vulnerability? How is it used in phishing attacks?
lessons.qsub: How do you prevent open redirects while still allowing legitimate redirects? What is the OAuth state parameter for?
terms: Trusted domain ka link, evil destination.
lessons.what: Definition: Login ke baad ?returnTo= par blindly redirect karna attacker ko trusted domain se phishing link banane deta hai, aur OAuth/SSO flows mein token leak ka raasta.
lessons.why: Chhoti bug lagti hai par phishing aur OAuth code theft chain mein use hoti hai.

lessons.name: Insecure Deserialization — object injection, remote code execution
lessons.desc: Insecure deserialization: untrusted data is deserialized into objects without validation. Can lead to remote code execution (Java RCE, PHP object injection). Mitigation: avoid deserializing untrusted data, use signed/encrypted serialization, integrity checks.
lessons.q: What is insecure deserialization and how does it lead to RCE?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between serialization and deserialization? How do you secure Java deserialization?
terms: Existing classes ko jod ke code execution.
lessons.what: Definition: Untrusted data ko native deserializer (Java ObjectInputStream, Python pickle, PHP unserialize) se load karna attacker ko object banane/methods chalane deta hai — aksar RCE.
lessons.why: Log4Shell-jaisi bugs aur Java/Python RCEs ka bada source.
lessons.code:
# Bad
obj = pickle.loads(request.data)
# Good
data = json.loads(request.data)
validate(data, SCHEMA)          # jsonschema / pydantic

# Agar zaroori ho: signed payload (HMAC) verify karke hi deserialize
cons: Legacy systems mein native serialization chala aa raha hota hai
gotchas: Pickle kabhi untrusted data par nahi
Signing se pehle verify, baad mein deserialize

lessons.name: Clickjacking — UI redressing, X-Frame-Options, CSP frame-ancestors
lessons.desc: Clickjacking: attacker iframes victim site transparently, tricks user into clicking. Mitigation: X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN. CSP frame-ancestors directive (preferred). Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'. JavaScript frame-busting is bypassable.
lessons.q: What is clickjacking and how do you prevent it?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors? Why is JavaScript frame-busting not recommended?
lessons.what: Definition: Attacker tumhari site ko transparent iframe mein load karke apne page ke button ke upar rakh deta hai; user 'free gift' click karta hai par asal mein 'delete account' dabata hai.
lessons.why: One-click sensitive actions (payments, follow, delete) risk mein.
gotchas: JS frame-busting bypassable hai — header use karo
SameSite cookies bhi cross-site iframe mein session roakte hain
Embed chahiye to specific origins allow

lessons.name: Session-based vs Token-based Auth
lessons.desc: Sessions: server stores state, client gets cookie. Tokens (JWT): client stores claims, server validates signature. Access tokens (short-lived) vs refresh tokens (long-lived, rotated).
lessons.q: Compare session-based and token-based authentication. What are the trade-offs for scalability and security?
lessons.qsub: When would you choose opaque tokens over JWTs? How does refresh token rotation prevent replay attacks?
terms: Server state + cookie mein session ID.
lessons.what: Definition: Sessions server-side store (Redis) mein state rakhte hain, logout/revoke turant. JWT stateless hai, scale easy par revoke mushkil — short expiry + refresh token chahiye.
lessons.why: Browser apps ke liye HttpOnly cookie session aksar simple aur safer; microservices/mobile mein tokens.
gotchas: JWT ko localStorage mein rakhna XSS risk
Session fixation: login par ID rotate karo

lessons.name: JWT Deep Dive
lessons.desc: Three base64url segments: header, payload, signature. Common attacks: alg=none, algorithm confusion, weak HMAC secret. Always validate signature, expiry, issuer, and audience.
lessons.q: Explain the alg=none attack on JWTs. How do you prevent algorithm confusion attacks?
lessons.qsub: Why should you use RS256/ES256 over HS256? How does storing JWTs in HttpOnly cookies prevent XSS-based token theft?
terms: RS256 public key ko HS256 secret banana.
lessons.what: Definition: JWT = header.payload.signature (base64url). Payload encrypted nahi, sirf signed hai. Verify karte waqt algorithm pin karo aur exp, iss, aud check karo.
lessons.why: JWT misuse auth bypass ka common raasta hai.
gotchas: Weak HS256 secret brute-force ho sakta hai

lessons.name: OAuth 2.0 & OIDC
lessons.desc: OAuth 2.0: delegated authorization via access tokens. Authorization Code Flow with PKCE prevents interception. OIDC adds id_token (JWT) for authentication on top of OAuth.
lessons.q: Walk through the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Why is PKCE necessary?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between an access token and an ID token? Why was the Implicit Flow deprecated?
terms: Authorization code interception se bachata hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Authorization Code + PKCE flow: app user ko IdP par bhejti hai → code milta hai → backend/SPA code+verifier se token leta hai. OAuth authZ hai; login ke liye OIDC ID token.
lessons.why: Third-party login aur API delegation ka standard; implicit flow ab deprecated.
gotchas: state check na karo to CSRF
Access token ≠ identity; ID token validate karo

lessons.name: SAML & Enterprise SSO
lessons.desc: XML-based SSO protocol. IdP authenticates user and sends signed SAML assertion to SP. Used by Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin. Vulnerable to XML signature wrapping and response replay.
lessons.q: How does SP-initiated SAML SSO work? What are the security risks in SAML assertions?
lessons.qsub: Compare SAML and OIDC for enterprise SSO. When would you recommend OIDC over SAML for a new integration?
terms: Signed XML jisme user identity hai.
lessons.what: Definition: SAML enterprise SSO: user SP se IdP par redirect, login, IdP signed assertion bhejta hai, SP signature verify karke session banata hai.
lessons.why: B2B customers ka common requirement.
lessons.code:
SP -> user -> IdP (AuthnRequest)
IdP -> user -> SP (POST SAMLResponse, signed)
SP: verify signature, Audience, NotOnOrAfter, InResponseTo
gotchas: Signature wrapping attacks — maintained library use karo

lessons.name: Passwordless & MFA
lessons.desc: WebAuthn/FIDO2: browser-based public key auth, no shared secret. Passkeys sync across devices via iCloud/Google. TOTP: time-based 6-digit codes. Phishing-resistant > phishable.
lessons.q: How does WebAuthn work at a technical level? Why are passkeys considered the future of authentication?
lessons.qsub: Compare TOTP, SMS, push notifications, and WebAuthn for MFA. Why is SMS the weakest option?
terms: Kuch jaante ho + kuch ho + kuch ho.
lessons.what: Definition: WebAuthn mein private key device par rehti hai, server sirf public key rakhta hai — phishing-resistant kyunki credential origin se bound hai. TOTP/SMS kamzor, push fatigue ka risk.
lessons.why: Passwords leak/phish hote hain; passkeys inhe hata dete hain.
gotchas: SMS OTP SIM-swap se toot-ta hai
Recovery path hi weakest link ban sakta hai

lessons.name: Secure Development Lifecycle
lessons.desc: SDL integrates security into every phase: design (threat model) → code (SAST) → test (DAST) → deploy (scan) → operate (monitor). A bug in design costs $100; in production, $100K+.
lessons.q: How do you integrate security into a CI/CD pipeline? What tools do you use at each stage?
lessons.qsub: Compare SAST, DAST, and IAST. When would you use each? What are the limitations of static analysis?
terms: Security ko early phases mein laana.
Code scan / running app scan / dependency scan.
lessons.what: Definition: SDL: requirements → threat model → secure coding + SAST → DAST/pen-test → release gate → monitoring. CI mein automated checks.
lessons.why: Production mein bug fix 10-100x mahanga hota hai.
lessons.code:
# CI pipeline
steps:
  - run: npm audit --audit-level=high      # SCA
  - run: semgrep --config auto .           # SAST
  - run: gitleaks detect                   # secrets
  - run: zap-baseline.py -t $STAGING_URL   # DAST
gotchas: Tools alerts ko triage karo warna ignore ho jaate hain
Gate sirf high severity par shuru karo

lessons.name: Secrets Management
lessons.desc: Never store secrets in code, config files, or cleartext env vars. Use HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager for storage, rotation, and just-in-time access with automatic expiry.
lessons.q: How do you manage database credentials and API keys in a microservices architecture?
lessons.qsub: What is envelope encryption in Vault? How does just-in-time access reduce the blast radius of credential compromise?
lessons.what: Definition: Code/git/Docker image mein secrets nahi. Runtime par vault se inject, IAM role se access, rotate, audit. Leak hone par turant revoke.
lessons.why: GitHub par leaked keys minutes mein bots exploit karte hain.
gotchas: Env vars logs/crash dumps mein leak ho sakte hain

lessons.name: Container Security
lessons.desc: Scan images for CVEs (Trivy, Grype), run as non-root, use minimal base images (distroless). K8s: Pod Security Standards, Network Policies, OPA Gatekeeper policies.
lessons.q: How do you secure a Kubernetes cluster from image build to runtime?
lessons.qsub: What is a container escape? How do Pod Security Standards and seccomp profiles prevent it?
lessons.what: Definition: Minimal base image, non-root user, read-only filesystem, capabilities drop, no privileged containers, signed images aur registry scanning.
lessons.why: Container escape aur vulnerable packages common attack path hain.
lessons.code:
FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20
COPY --chown=nonroot:nonroot app /app
USER nonroot

# k8s
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
gotchas: Latest tag pin nahi hota — digest use karo
Secrets image layers mein reh jaate hain

lessons.name: API Security
lessons.desc: Authenticate every request, authorize every operation, validate every input, rate limit per client. CORS restricts cross-origin access. APIs are the #1 modern attack vector.
lessons.q: How would you secure a public REST API serving millions of requests per day?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement rate limiting effectively? Compare API keys vs JWTs for machine-to-machine vs user auth.
lessons.what: Definition: Har request authN, har operation authZ, input schema validation, rate limit, TLS, proper error messages (no stack traces), logging.
lessons.why: APIs ab primary attack surface hain (OWASP API Top 10).
lessons.code:
const schema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), qty: z.number().int().min(1).max(100) });
app.post('/orders', limiter, authenticate, validate(schema), handler);

lessons.name: Dependency & Supply Chain Security
lessons.desc: SCA scans dependencies for CVEs. SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) inventories all components. Artifact signing (cosign) and SLSA levels secure the build pipeline against attacks like SolarWinds.
lessons.q: How do you protect against supply chain attacks in your software development process?
lessons.qsub: What is dependency confusion? How do SBOMs and SLSA levels help defend against attacks like SolarWinds and log4j?
lessons.what: Definition: Dependencies mein CVEs, typosquatting, malicious updates. Defense: lockfiles, SCA, SBOM, signed artifacts (Sigstore), minimal deps, private registry.
lessons.why: Log4Shell, event-stream jaise incidents supply chain se aaye.
lessons.code:
$ npm ci                      # lockfile exact install
$ npm audit --omit=dev
$ syft . -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
$ cosign verify <image>

lessons.name: IAM & Least Privilege
lessons.desc: IAM manages identities and permissions. Service accounts for machines. Policy conditions restrict by IP, time, MFA. Start minimal, add only what is needed. Never use wildcard actions.
lessons.q: How do you design IAM policies for a multi-service cloud application?
lessons.qsub: What are permission boundaries? How does AWS Access Analyzer detect unauthorized resource sharing?
terms: Services roles use karein, long-lived keys nahi.
lessons.what: Definition: IAM identities (users, roles, service accounts) ko policies deti hai. Wildcard * avoid karo, roles assume karo, MFA, permission boundaries, access review.
lessons.why: Over-permissioned role ek bug ko poore cloud takeover mein badal deta hai.
lessons.code:
{ "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/reports/*",
  "Condition": { "Bool": { "aws:SecureTransport": "true" } } }

lessons.name: Network Security
lessons.desc: VPC isolates networks with public/private subnets across AZs. Security Groups (stateful), NACLs (stateless), WAF (L7 SQLi/XSS), and Shield/CloudFront for DDoS protection.
lessons.q: Design a VPC architecture for a three-tier web application. What security controls apply at each layer?
lessons.qsub: When would you use NACLs in addition to Security Groups? How does WAF rate-based rule differ from Shield Advanced?
lessons.what: Definition: DBs private subnet mein, sirf LB public. SG least-open, NAT egress, VPC endpoints, WAF, flow logs.
lessons.why: Network segmentation lateral movement rokta hai.
lessons.code:
SG db: inbound 5432 FROM sg-app only
SG app: inbound 443 FROM sg-alb only
0.0.0.0/0 inbound sirf ALB:443

lessons.name: Data Protection
lessons.desc: Encryption at rest (AES-256 on S3, RDS, EBS) and in transit (TLS 1.3). KMS manages keys with automatic rotation. Envelope encryption: KMS encrypts DEK, DEK encrypts data.
lessons.q: How do you implement encryption at rest and in transit for a cloud-native application?
lessons.qsub: What is envelope encryption? When would you need CloudHSM instead of KMS for key management?
lessons.what: Definition: Data classification, encryption at rest (KMS keys) aur in transit, backups encrypted, tokenization PII, retention policies.
lessons.why: Breach hone par encrypted data useless hota hai (agar keys safe hon).
lessons.code:
aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket b --server-side-encryption-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault":{"SSEAlgorithm":"aws:kms"}}]}'
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket b --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,...

lessons.name: Compliance & Audit
lessons.desc: SOC2 (5 trust criteria), HIPAA (PHI protection), GDPR (EU data rights), PCI DSS (card data). Audit logging (CloudTrail), automated evidence collection (Vanta, Drata).
lessons.q: How do you design a system that is compliant by default for SOC2 and GDPR?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between SOC2 Type I and Type II? How do you handle GDPR right to erasure in a distributed system?
lessons.what: Definition: Compliance frameworks controls aur evidence maangte hain: access reviews, logging, change management, incident response, data retention, right to erasure (GDPR).
lessons.why: Enterprise sales aur legal requirements.
lessons.code:
Evidence automation:
- IAM access review quarterly
- CloudTrail enabled, immutable logs
- Backups tested
- Vendor risk assessments

lessons.name: Incident Response
lessons.desc: IR phases: Preparation → Detection → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Postmortem. Runbooks define steps per scenario. Blameless postmortems focus on process failures, not people.
lessons.q: Walk through your incident response process for a suspected data breach in a cloud environment.
lessons.qsub: How do you contain an active breach? What goes into a blameless postmortem and how do you prevent recurrence?
terms: Prepare, Detect, Contain, Eradicate, Recover, Lessons.
lessons.what: Definition: Detect → triage severity → contain (isolate, revoke creds) → eradicate (root cause) → recover → postmortem. Evidence preserve karo, communication plan rakho.
lessons.why: Taiyari se response minutes mein hota hai, ghanto mein nahi.
lessons.code:
Compromised key runbook:
1. Key disable/rotate
2. CloudTrail se use dekho
3. Affected resources isolate
4. Notify (legal/customers if needed)
5. Postmortem + action items

lessons.name: Zero Trust Architecture
lessons.desc: "Never trust, always verify" — no implicit trust based on network location. Micro-segmentation per service. Continuous verification on every sensitive operation. Google BeyondCorp pioneered this.
lessons.q: How would you implement Zero Trust architecture in an existing cloud application?
lessons.qsub: How does Google BeyondCorp differ from traditional VPN-based access? What role does Identity-Aware Proxy play?
lessons.what: Definition: Perimeter model toot gaya (remote work, cloud). Zero trust mein har request authenticate+authorize, mTLS, device health, least privilege.
lessons.why: Attacker andar aa jaaye to flat network sab khol deta hai.
lessons.code:
# mTLS between services (Istio)
PeerAuthentication: mtls.mode = STRICT
AuthorizationPolicy: allow frontend -> orders only

lessons.name: Secure by Design
lessons.desc: Security is part of every component decision, not bolted on. Patterns: least privilege, defense in depth, fail secure, secure defaults, complete mediation, economy of mechanism.
lessons.q: What does "Secure by Design" mean in practice? Give examples of each principle in a real system.
lessons.qsub: How does "fail secure" differ from "fail open"? When would you choose one over the other in a distributed system?
lessons.what: Definition: Security architecture ka hissa: minimize attack surface, least privilege, separation of duties, safe defaults, input validation boundary par.
lessons.why: Bolt-on security fragile hoti hai.
lessons.code:
Design checklist:
- Auth boundary kahan?
- Sensitive data kahan flow karta hai?
- Failure mode kya (open/closed)?
- Audit trail?

lessons.name: Cryptography in Practice
lessons.desc: TLS 1.3: 1-RTT handshake, 3 cipher suites only. AEAD (AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). ECDHE for perfect forward secrecy. X25519 preferred over P-256 for key exchange.
lessons.q: Explain the TLS 1.3 handshake. How does it improve security and performance over TLS 1.2?
lessons.qsub: What is perfect forward secrecy and why is ECDHE essential? Compare GCM vs ChaCha20-Poly1305 for different hardware.
lessons.what: Definition: TLS 1.3 sirf strong cipher suites rakhta hai, ECDHE se forward secrecy. Practical: HSTS, cert automation, mTLS internal, disable TLS 1.0/1.1.
lessons.why: Misconfiguration (weak ciphers, missing HSTS) real-world mein common.
lessons.code:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

# nginx
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
$ testssl.sh example.com

lessons.name: Security Monitoring & SIEM
lessons.desc: SIEM aggregates logs from all sources, normalizes, correlates, and alerts. SOAR automates incident response. Detection engineering writes rules as code. Median dwell time without SIEM: 204 days.
lessons.q: How do you design a security monitoring strategy for a cloud-native application?
lessons.qsub: What correlation rules would you write to detect a compromised IAM credential? How does SOAR reduce response time?
lessons.what: Definition: Auth logs, CloudTrail, app logs ek jagah; rules (impossible travel, many failed logins, new admin) alert deti hain; triage aur runbooks.
lessons.why: Detect nahi kiya to breach mahino chalta hai.
lessons.code:
rule: >10 failed logins / 5 min per user -> alert
rule: IAM policy change outside CI -> high severity
log: who, what, when, where (never passwords/tokens)
gotchas: Log tampering se bachne ke liye immutable storage

lessons.name: BOLA — Broken Object Level Authorization
lessons.desc: BOLA (formerly IDOR) is the #1 API vulnerability. Attacker accesses objects by manipulating IDs in API calls (e.g., /api/users/123 → /api/users/456). Server doesn't verify ownership. Most common in REST APIs.
lessons.q: What is BOLA? How do you prevent it in a multi-tenant API?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between BOLA and broken function level authorization? How do row-level security policies help?
terms: Object id badal ke dusre ka object.
lessons.what: Definition: GET /orders/123 ko 124 karke dusre user ka order mil jaye to BOLA. Fix: har object access par user-ownership/policy check.
lessons.why: API Top 10 #1 — sabse common aur impactful.

lessons.name: Broken Authentication — credential stuffing, session fixation, weak JWT
lessons.desc: Broken Authentication encompasses weak passwords, no rate limiting on login, credential stuffing, session fixation, and weak JWT implementation (alg:none, no expiry, weak secret).
lessons.q: How do you prevent credential stuffing attacks on a login API? What makes a JWT implementation insecure?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between session fixation and session hijacking? How does MFA mitigate credential stuffing?
terms: Attacker ki session ID victim par.
lessons.what: Definition: Weak passwords, no throttling, predictable tokens, long-lived JWT, no MFA. Fix: MFA, breached-password check, lockout/backoff, rotate session ID after login.
lessons.why: Account takeover seedha users ko hit karta hai.

lessons.name: Broken Object Property Level Authorization — mass assignment, excessive data exposure
lessons.desc: Mass assignment: API accepts all fields from request body, allowing attackers to set unintended properties (e.g., isAdmin: true). Excessive data exposure: API returns more fields than the client needs.
lessons.q: What is mass assignment? How do you prevent it in a REST API?
lessons.qsub: How does field filtering (DTOs, GraphQL selection sets) prevent excessive data exposure? What is the principle of least data?
terms: Request body ke saare fields model mein.
lessons.what: Definition: User.update(req.body) se attacker isAdmin:true bhej sakta hai. Response mein password hash/internal fields chale jaate hain.
lessons.why: Privilege escalation bina kisi complex exploit ke.

lessons.name: Unrestricted Resource Consumption — rate limiting, pagination, resource limits
lessons.desc: APIs without rate limiting are vulnerable to DoS. Lack of pagination allows fetching millions of records. No file size limits enable storage abuse. No query complexity limits enable GraphQL abuse.
lessons.q: How do you implement rate limiting for a public API? What are the tradeoffs between different rate limiting algorithms?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between fixed window, sliding window, and token bucket rate limiting? How do you rate limit GraphQL queries?
lessons.what: Definition: APIs bina limits ke DoS aur bill-shock ka shikaar hote hain: huge page size, expensive queries, large uploads, SMS/email spam.
lessons.why: Availability aur cloud cost dono ka risk.
gotchas: Expensive endpoints par alag tight limits

lessons.name: Broken Function Level Authorization — admin endpoints, vertical privilege escalation
lessons.desc: Regular users accessing admin functions by calling admin API endpoints directly. Missing authorization checks on function-level operations. Vertical privilege escalation: low-privilege user gains admin access.
lessons.q: How do you prevent regular users from accessing admin API endpoints? What is vertical vs horizontal privilege escalation?
lessons.qsub: How do RBAC and ABAC differ for function-level authorization? What is the risk of exposing admin endpoints in a microservices architecture?
lessons.what: Definition: Normal user /api/admin/users ya DELETE method call kar leta hai kyunki sirf UI chhupaya gaya tha. Fix: server-side role/permission check central middleware mein.
lessons.why: UI hiding security nahi hai.
lessons.code:
app.use('/api/admin', authenticate, requireRole('admin'));
function requireRole(r){ return (req,res,next) => req.user.roles.includes(r) ? next() : res.sendStatus(403); }
gotchas: Tests mein low-privileged user se call karo
